title: mentha procumbens var. ruralis
intro: Mentha procumbens var. ruralis, commonly known as American Wild Bergamot, is a perennial herb belonging to the mint family (Lamiaceae). It is native to North America and has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and carminative properties. The bioactive constituents of American Wild Bergamot include menthone, menthyl acetate, and other volatile oils, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as reducing stress, improving digestion, and relieving respiratory issues. The plant's leaves and flowers can be used in teas, infusions, and essential oils to harness its benefits.
